post.originalText:
GPT-6 ASTRA + HIGGSFIELD BUILT THIS $35,000 SITE IN 5 STEPS. HERE IS THE WHOLE ANIMATION PIPELINE, WITH THE PROMPTS.

the first time I put video on a client site I wrote a description, hit generate, and got back something beautiful that had nothing to do with the brand..

after enough of those I stopped writing descriptions altogether. 

now I build the first frame and the last frame myself, sit with them a while, and the model only moves between them.

it hasn't surprised me badly since, and I miss the surprises less than I expected to.

"STEP 1. WRITE THE SHOT LIST BEFORE ANY PIXELS"

in Astra I open plan mode, agree the shot list there, and only then set it as a goal so it survives longer than one reply.

/plan

Six shots for a pre-launch aviation site. 

For each one give me the purpose, the first frame, the last frame and the length in seconds. 

No shot longer than 8 seconds.

/goal

Hold this shot list. 

Every image and every clip we make from now on belongs to one of these six.

the goal sits above the composer with its own progress, so nothing drifts into shot seven at two in the morning.

"STEP 2. PUT THE LOOK IN A FILE, NOT IN YOUR PROMPTS"

/init writes an AGENTS.md scaffold, and the visual contract goes in there once instead of into every prompt forever.

Look contract. 

Dawn or dusk only, never midday. 

Warm key from one side, cool ambient fill. Real camera behaviour, no floating drone moves. 

Six rotors on the aircraft, white body, dark underside. 

Never restate this to me, just obey it.

the first long build I did, I pasted the style paragraph into
nineteen prompts and shot six still went its own way. 

it was not the model losing the thread, it was me never writing the thread down..

"STEP 3. BUILD THE MACHINE ONCE, THEN BUILD THE LAST FRAME"

the aircraft is invented, so nothing in the world keeps it
consistent, and that is why every fresh clip hands you a slightly different vehicle. 

it gets rendered once, and that file becomes the law.

generate with cinematic_studio_2_5, 16:9, 4k:
a white six rotor electric air taxi parked on a desert
pad, three quarter view from the front left, dark
underside, tilting rotors, dusk light from camera right,
long shadows, photographic, no people.

then comes the habit that changed the most for me. 

decide what the shot has to end on, build that still first, and only then build the opening frame that has to arrive at it.

generate with nano_banana_pro, 21:9, 4k, reference: aircraft_master.png: end frame. 

The aircraft is airborne at about fifty metres, rotors forward, city skyline low behind it, sunrise haze. 

Same vehicle as the reference, same livery, same six rotors.

a shot built forwards wanders, and a shot built backwards lands.

"STEP 4. BUY THE MOVEMENT, NOTHING ELSE"

now the video model gets both ends and has almost no room left to invent. 

audio goes off at generation, because a hero video only
autoplays if it is silent, and 21:9 means you are not cropping your own composition later.

generate with cinematic_studio_3_0, start_image: pad_start.png, end_image: air_end.png, 21:9, 1080p, generate_audio: false, 8 seconds: the aircraft lifts off the pad, rotors tilting forward as it rises, camera locked off on a tripod, thin low dust, one continuous take, no cuts, no camera shake.

"STEP 5. STRIP THE SKY AND BIND IT TO SCROLL"

where the machine floats over the page background instead of over a photograph, the clip runs with its background removed by video_background_remover.

that hands you the vehicle alone, so the section colour behind it can change without regenerating a single frame, and the file gets small enough that the hero still loads fast..

and when I want to try the reckless version of a shot, /side opens a temporary chat so the experiment never lands in the thread that holds the real build

five steps, and honestly only two of them are creative. 

the other three exist so that the creative two never have to be repeated nineteen times.
